page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Cache sizing consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance features no local storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistent storage.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional single-core processing capabilities. Single-core stress-ng tests place the CPU in the top 10% with a score of 3753.78, mirrored by top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 41.15 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.83 GB/sec. When executing multi-threaded tasks, performance normalizes to the median 50%, with stress-ng reaching 29877.07 and multi-threaded bzip3 achieving 125.95 GB/sec. Large uncached memory transfers deliver 61.1 GB/sec read and 44.55 GB/sec write throughput. The instance also handles lightweight machine learning inference efficiently, achieving top-tier text generation on small 135M parameter models at 351.12 tokens per second, while medium 7B model generation settles into the middle tier at 12.22 tokens per second.

The F8ams_v7 pairs high clock frequency with an expanded 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, offering strong compute efficiency for workloads that demand substantial memory capacity per thread without paying for excessive core counts. The dedicated single-threaded core layout prevents hyper-threading resource contention, although overall multi-core parallel throughput remains constrained by the 8-core ceiling. The absence of local temporary NVMe storage necessitates reliance on remote Azure storage volumes, shifting disk I/O performance to network capabilities. This server is best suited for memory-intensive computational jobs, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving environments requiring single-threaded responsiveness.
description: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v7 is a compute and memory-intensive virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Equipped with 8 dedicated physical cores running 8 single-threaded vCPUs, it provides 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware-level cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPUs, requiring remote storage volumes. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier single-threaded performance, with exceptional single-core stress-ng metrics, rapid gzip compression, and responsive small-model LLM generation, complemented by solid mid-range multi-core and memory throughput. Operating with dedicated CPU allocation, the configuration eliminates hyper-threading contention. The server fits memory-intensive applications requiring strong single-thread execution, including relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, ETL pipelines, and high-performance web servers.
